why: The answer applies the widening rule and the narrowing-cast rule to two specific lines of the code (d = i and the 9.99 to int line), giving a reason for one of them; it does not cover the other conversions (q, r, p, t) and does not link the two rules into one principle based on range or information loss, so it is a correct L2 answer that is incomplete.

concepts.quote: d = i happens by itself because double is bigger; going from 9.99 to int needs (int)
concepts.why: It correctly marks the int-to-double assignment as automatic and the double-to-int line as needing a cast, line by line, but leaves out the other conversion lines.
It describes double as the wider type, which is one correct point, but goes no further.
It names int as the target of the narrowing conversion and says nothing else about int.
It states correctly that a narrowing conversion needs a cast, but does not give the resulting value 9 or deal with the casts on q and r.
The answer makes no claim about data types in general.
